title: Exchange: High Volume Email can send to external recipients
summary: The briefing correctly separates the planned external-sending feature from today's internal-only HVE service and its documented billing. The billing-policy navigation reaches the correct tab but should specify selecting a policy from its drop-down menu.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft plans to extend HVE in Exchange Online to deliver email to external recipients, including customers and partners.
claims.quote: High Volume Email (HVE) External Sending extends HVE in Exchange Online, which today sends only to recipients inside your organization, so it can also deliver bulk email to external recipients such as customers and partners.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn currently documents HVE as internal-only and unable to deliver external email.
claims.quote: HVE accounts cannot be used for external email delivery.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The planned feature is intended for operational and transactional messages such as notifications, alerts and receipts.
claims.quote: It is designed for operational and transactional messages, like notifications, alerts, receipts and required communications, and not for marketing campaigns.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The roadmap says the feature is not for marketing campaigns.
claims.quote: It is designed for operational and transactional messages, like notifications, alerts, receipts and required communications, and not for marketing campaigns.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Apps and devices submit messages through SMTP.
claims.quote: Apps and devices send through SMTP using HVE account authentication.

claims.quote: Apps and devices send through SMTP using HVE account authentication.

claims.claim: External sending is admin-opt-in, so leaving it unenabled preserves internal-only sending rather than automatically changing ordinary users' behaviour.
claims.quote: Admins turn the feature on for specific HVE accounts with a cmdlet.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the planned external-sending feature.
claims.quote: Searched: High Volume Email external recipients enable cmdlet settings external sending quotas throttling suppression content controls pricing prerequisites. Opened Manage High Volume Email; read HVE SMTP error excerpts. Both still say external delivery is unsupported.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and controls[0].api; What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No Exchange admin center setting or Exchange PowerShell command for enabling external sending on an HVE account is documented yet.
claims.quote: Searched: High Volume Email external sending enable Exchange PowerShell Set-HVEAccountSettings. Opened Manage High Volume Email, Set-HVEAccountSettings and Set-HVEAccountBillingPolicy; found ReplyTo and billing mapping, not an external-sending switch.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has not documented content controls specifically for the planned external HVE mail service.
claims.quote: Searched: High Volume Email data loss prevention mail flow rules. Read mail-flow-rule and DLP search excerpts and the full HVE page; general Exchange controls are described, but external HVE is not placed within their documented processing.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Throttling values for external HVE sending are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: High Volume Email external quota throttling limits. Read Exchange Online limits and outbound-sending-limit excerpts; opened Manage High Volume Email. Its limits expressly cover internal-only HVE, not the planned external service.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: Quota values for external HVE sending are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: High Volume Email external quota throttling limits. Read Exchange Online limits and outbound-sending-limit excerpts; opened Manage High Volume Email. No external HVE quota is stated; the HVE table specifies internal recipients only.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Values governing suppression of problem recipients for external HVE mail are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: High Volume Email suppression list; High Volume Email external recipients content controls DLP mail flow rules suppression list quotas throttling. Read ACS and Customer Insights suppression excerpts and the HVE page; none states external HVE suppression thresholds.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published whether administrators can adjust the external-sending throttling, quota or suppression controls.
claims.quote: Searched: High Volume Email external quota throttling limits; High Volume Email suppression list. Opened the HVE page and Set-HVEAccountSettings; read limits and suppression search excerpts. No external HVE adjustment control was documented.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no suppression-list management control for external HVE mail as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: High Volume Email suppression list. Read ACS managed suppression, ACS opt-out management and Customer Insights suppression excerpts; opened the HVE page and Set-HVEAccountSettings. The other products' controls are not documented for external HVE.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: HVE currently supports basic authentication and OAuth for SMTP connections.
claims.quote: High Volume Email supports both modern authentication (OAuth) and basic authentication for SMTP connections.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends using OAuth when possible rather than basic authentication for HVE.
claims.quote: Use OAuth authentication when possible. OAuth provides stronger security and better alignment with modern authentication practices.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Enabling Microsoft Entra ID Security Defaults disables basic authentication, including SMTP.
claims.quote: If Security Defaults are enabled in Microsoft Entra ID, all basic authentication methods (including SMTP) are disabled.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: With Security Defaults enabled, HVE can authenticate only through OAuth.
claims.quote: In this configuration, HVE can authenticate only by using OAuth.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: An HVE account uses an email address in a domain accepted in the tenant, supporting the warning about external sends under the organisation's domain.
claims.quote: Primary email address – Must use a domain that’s accepted in your tenant (for example, hve-app@contoso.com).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: HVE is an automated application-and-device messaging service rather than a workflow requiring a person to approve each message.
claims.quote: HVE is designed for automated, transactional and operational messaging. It uses dedicated HVE accounts instead of user or shared mailboxes

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; controls[1].note; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: HVE uses Microsoft 365 pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: High Volume Email uses M365 pay as you go (PAYG) billing.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: For current HVE, Microsoft 365 pay-as-you-go billing must be configured for the tenant before assigning a billing policy.
claims.quote: Before you assign a billing policy to an HVE account, ensure that Microsoft 365 pay as you go billing is set up for your tenant

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Each HVE account needs a billing policy linking it to the Azure subscription used for usage-based billing.
claims.quote: each HVE account must be associated with a billing policy, which links the account to an Azure subscription for usage based billing.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: An HVE account without a valid assigned billing policy cannot send email.
claims.quote: No billing policy is assigned, or there’s an issue with the assigned policy. The HVE account will not be able to send email, until a valid policy is assigned.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The published current HVE meter counts expanded delivered email recipients.
claims.quote: High Volume Email | Number of expanded delivered email recipients | $0.000042 per one recipient (equivalent to $42 per one million recipients)

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The current HVE rate is USD $0.000042 per recipient, equivalent to $42 per million recipients.
claims.quote: What's billed? (USD) | High Volume Email | Number of expanded delivered email recipients | $0.000042 per one recipient (equivalent to $42 per one million recipients)

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Recipients are counted for billing after distribution-list expansion.
claims.quote: However, for billing purposes, recipients are counted after distribution list expansion.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: HVE accounts do not require Microsoft 365 licences.
claims.quote: HVE accounts do not require Microsoft 365 licenses and shouldn’t be treated as user mailboxes.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft says not to assign licences to HVE accounts.
claims.quote: Do not assign licenses to HVE accounts.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A rate specifically for external HVE recipients, or confirmation that today's internal HVE rate applies, is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: High Volume Email external sending pricing licensing prerequisites pay as you go. Opened HVE and PAYG overview; read PAYG services and what's-new excerpts. They describe internal HVE; none specifies a rate for the planned external-recipient service.

claims.where: Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Prerequisites specific to the planned external-sending feature are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: High Volume Email external sending pricing licensing prerequisites pay as you go. Opened Manage High Volume Email and read HVE billing and test-prerequisite excerpts. These cover current internal HVE, not external preview eligibility or prerequisites.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Reply-To is the only account-setting change documented for Set-HVEAccountSettings in its current reference.
claims.quote:
Set-HVEAccountSettings
    [-Identity] <MailUserIdParameter>
    [-ReplyTo <SmtpAddress>]
    [-Confirm]
    [-WhatIf]
    [<CommonParameters>]

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Exchange admin center > Mail flow > High Volume Email > account > Billing policies reaches the billing-policy assignment page.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Mail flow, and then select High Volume Email. Select an HVE account from the list to open the account details. When you open an account, two tabs are available – General and Billing policies.
claims.fix: Keep the documented path and add to controls[1].note: 'On the Billing policies tab, select a different billing policy from the drop-down menu.' Apply the same addition to the rendered row note, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/mail-flow-best-practices/high-volume-mails-m365.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Exchange PowerShell Set-HVEAccountBillingPolicy -Identity <HVE account> -BillingPolicyId <billing policy GUID> assigns the policy to the specified account.
claims.quote: The BillingPolicyId parameter specified the GUID of the billing policy to assign to the HVE account. The Identity parameter specifies the email address of the HVE account you want to modify.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The documented billing-policy mapping control assigns payment configuration rather than selecting which recipients an account may email.
claims.quote: Use the Set-HVEAccountBillingPolicy cmdlet to modify the billing policy mapping for a specified High Volume Email (HVE) account.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model
claims.claim: The licensing model is consumption, consistent with HVE pay-as-you-go billing and the roadmap's per-external-recipient usage billing.
claims.quote: High Volume Email uses M365 pay as you go (PAYG) billing.

claims.where: front matter: cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The variable cost rating reflects the documented pay-as-you-go recipient meter rather than claiming no direct charge.
claims.quote: High Volume Email | Number of expanded delivered email recipients | $0.000042 per one recipient (equivalent to $42 per one million recipients)
